stories.body: The death toll from catastrophic flash flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border has risen to at least 389 in Nepal, while three deaths have been reported in Tibet, and more than 1,300 people remain missing. The disaster swept through mountain valleys, destroying villages, roads, bridges and power infrastructure in an area popular with trekkers and pilgrims. Hundreds of foreign visitors are among the missing, while helicopters and thousands of rescue personnel are searching isolated areas, evacuating survivors and delivering food, medicine and tents. Authorities also warned that a lake formed near the disaster site was rising and could pose a further risk.
stories.headline: Nepal-Tibet floods kill hundreds as more than 1,300 remain missing

stories.body: Scientists and the US Geological Survey say a glacial collapse, rather than an earthquake, appears to have caused the devastating flooding on the Nepal-Tibet border. A large mass of ice, rock and debris is believed to have broken away near Langtang Lirung and entered a tributary river, producing a sudden debris-filled surge that raised downstream river levels by as much as nine metres in about 30 minutes. The impact registered as a seismic event, contributing to initial confusion about the cause. Experts say the area’s extremely steep terrain likely amplified the flood, while the underlying cause of the unusually large glacier collapse remains unclear.
stories.headline: Glacial collapse believed to have triggered catastrophic Nepal-Tibet flooding

stories.body: Qatar's prime minister visited Tehran for talks aimed at de-escalating the conflict between Iran and the United States and addressing the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway, which previously carried more than one-fifth of global oil and gas supplies, has been largely shut to shipping since early March, disrupting energy markets. Qatar, Oman and Pakistan have all sent senior delegations to Tehran in recent days as mediators seek a return to negotiations. Iran and Oman have discussed a temporary shipping route, but Tehran says the strait will not fully reopen unless the United States lifts sanctions and unfreezes Iranian assets.
stories.headline: Iran and Qatar hold talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz amid US blockade

stories.body: Ratko Mladić, the former Bosnian Serb military commander convicted of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, has died in a United Nations prison hospital in The Hague at age 84. Mladić was serving a life sentence imposed in 2017 and upheld on appeal in 2021 for crimes during the 1992-95 Bosnian war, including the 1995 killing of more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys at Srebrenica and the siege of Sarajevo. The UN tribunal said an inquiry had been ordered into the circumstances of his death. Survivors said his death could not bring closure, while some Serbian nationalist figures continued to praise him.
stories.headline: Ratko Mladić, convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre, dies aged 84

stories.body: Meta has agreed to pay up to $18 billion over 10 years to settle a landmark case brought by 48 US states alleging that Facebook and Instagram harmed children and encouraged addictive use. The settlement requires stronger safeguards for users under 18, including night curfews and two-hour usage limits, alongside other changes to the platforms. The litigation included claims that Meta failed to verify ages adequately, exposed children to harmful content and collected data from children under 13 without proper parental consent. Meta denied wrongdoing, but the agreement may add to global pressure on social-media companies to strengthen child-safety protections.
stories.headline: Meta reaches multibillion-dollar settlement over harms to children

stories.body: ICE officer Christian Castro was released from custody in Texas after a federal judge rejected Minnesota's request to compel his extradition. Castro is charged in Minnesota with assault and falsely reporting a crime after prosecutors said he shot 24-year-old Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis through the front door of a Minneapolis home in January, then falsely claimed that Sosa-Celis and another man had attacked an ICE officer. Texas had held Castro since his May arrest, but state law required his release after 90 days unless extradition was granted. The judge said the case was not yet ripe because Governor Greg Abbott had not formally denied Minnesota's extradition request.
stories.headline: ICE agent charged in Minneapolis shooting released in Texas after Minnesota loses extradition bid

stories.body: A federal judge in California ruled that the Trump administration illegally reduced the wages of migrant farmworkers. The administration had said the policy was intended to offset the effects of its immigration policies, but the court found the wage cuts unlawful.
stories.headline: Federal judge rules Trump administration's migrant farmworker wage cuts illegal

stories.body: The Trump administration has paused immigrant-visa applications while consular officials are trained on a stricter public-charge policy intended to exclude people deemed likely to rely on public assistance. The State Department says the pause, which began in early August, should last only into September and primarily affects family-based visa applicants. The administration is also preparing to revoke the business and tourist visas of up to 200,000 people who applied for asylum, which would be the largest mass visa revocation in US history. Immigration experts say the measures reflect a broader effort to reduce legal as well as unauthorized immigration.
stories.headline: Trump administration expands immigration crackdown to people entering legally

stories.body: The Food and Drug Administration has approved Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib for pancreatic cancer after clinical trials showed the drug nearly doubled average survival times for patients with one of the deadliest forms of cancer.
stories.headline: FDA approves pancreatic cancer drug that significantly extends survival

stories.body: Tensions are escalating in Ceuta nearly a month after a mass arrival of migrants, with residents protesting proposed accommodation sites and clashes reported on beaches and in the Benzú district. Demonstrators tried to dismantle a Red Cross food-distribution camp and some pursued migrants from a beach, prompting police to use warning shots and smoke canisters. Authorities said a separate group of migrants later attacked a vehicle carrying four soldiers with stones, injuring the troops. Spain's government says it is working to restore normality and has denied having advance knowledge of the scale of the mass arrivals, which it says were fueled by misinformation on social media.
stories.headline: Ceuta tensions escalate as police, migrants and residents clash during migration crisis

stories.body: Spanish police have detained 12 Moroccan migrants over an alleged ambush on a military vehicle in Ceuta's Benzú district that injured four soldiers. Authorities said a group of 30 to 40 people surrounded the vehicle before throwing stones, causing serious damage; the soldiers fled on foot but were reportedly pursued with sticks and large rocks until police intervened. The incident occurred amid wider unrest following the mass crossing into Ceuta nearly a month ago, and police said further arrests were possible.
stories.headline: Twelve migrants detained after stone attack injures four soldiers in Ceuta

stories.body: Spain's autonomous regions approved a €25 million transfer to Ceuta to help care for unaccompanied migrant children following July's mass arrivals, although several regional governments said the funding was inadequate. Fourteen regions backed the payment, while Aragón, Castilla y León and Extremadura did not participate. The meeting did not resolve the politically contentious question of redistributing children from Ceuta to other parts of Spain. The government says family reunification in Morocco is the preferred option, but acknowledges that return will not be possible in many cases and that Spain must provide care.
stories.headline: Spain's regions approve €25 million in aid for Ceuta but remain divided over relocating migrant children

stories.body: A wildfire in the protected Devesa forest area of El Saler, near Valencia's Albufera lagoon, prompted the preventive evacuation of the village, nearby campsites and beach areas after a change in wind direction pushed the fire toward residential zones. Authorities activated a level-two wildfire emergency plan, closed access roads and sent mobile alerts directing evacuees toward Valencia. Firefighters, aerial resources, police and the Military Emergency Unit were deployed, while shelters were opened for residents and campers.
stories.headline: Wildfire forces evacuation of El Saler and nearby campsites outside Valencia

stories.body: Thieves stole most of the Treasure of Villena, one of Europe's most important Bronze Age gold hoards, in a raid lasting only a few minutes at the Villena Museum in Alicante province. The collection of 66 mainly gold artifacts, dating to around 1000 BC, includes bracelets, bowls and bottles and has an estimated gold value of at least €1.7 million, though officials described its heritage value as incalculable. Investigators believe several people using multiple vehicles entered through a window, and are examining whether an alarm at a sports center shortly before the break-in was a deliberate diversion.
stories.headline: Bronze Age Treasure of Villena stolen in rapid museum heist

stories.body: Barcelona City Council is removing publications containing the personal and workplace details of 568 Guardia Urbana officers after police unions complained to the Catalan data-protection authority. The documents had made officers' names, professional identification numbers, units, work locations and shifts accessible online through the Municipal Gazette. Unions said the combined information could enable officers to be tracked and put them and their families at risk. The council said it would immediately take down the affected records, search for similar documents and change future publication practices, while insisting the incident was not an external data breach.
stories.headline: Barcelona removes personal and work data for 568 Guardia Urbana officers after privacy complaint

stories.body: Barcelona Oberta, an association representing central commercial and tourist districts, says visitor numbers and sales fell across many major shopping areas this summer compared with last year, despite strong tourism in the city. The group attributes the decline to simultaneous roadworks that have disrupted access and movement, including projects around Plaça d'Espanya, Gran Via, Meridiana, Glòries, the Ronda de Dalt and the L8 extension. It says the effects have been especially severe in areas such as La Rambla, Glòries and Sants, and is calling for better coordination of works and fewer mobility restrictions from September.
stories.headline: Barcelona's central commercial districts report lower summer visitor numbers and sales

stories.body: Barcelona's Boqueria market will require every stall to retain at least 50% traditional food products under a new internal regulation intended to reduce tourist-oriented prepared offerings and draw local shoppers back. The rule is expected to be approved before the end of the year and accompanies a €12 million modernization project. Smaller works, including new public toilets and improvements to logistics lighting, are expected to begin this autumn, while the main renovation of the fish section and the roof and façade is scheduled for 2027 to 2029. Market officials say the changes are intended to preserve the Boqueria's character as a food market rather than a tourist attraction.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Boqueria market plans reforms to curb tourist-oriented offerings

stories.body: Barcelona's Les Corts-Can Bruixa weather station has recorded 52 torrid nights this year, surpassing the previous record set in 2003. Nearly one in three of those nights had a minimum temperature above 27°C, underscoring the persistence of exceptionally high overnight heat in the city.
stories.headline: Barcelona records a new nocturnal heat record as torrid nights continue
